story: Completing the next token of a famous British name or place (Tower of London, Trafalgar, Regent, Hampton Court) where the first fragment already implies the rest.
Completing the all-caps category label 'HISTORIC BUILDING' that heads guidebook listing entries.
Predicting the first price digit immediately after a pound sign in a listing (mains £[12], £[6].50).
Predicting listing-line formatting: the double-space spacer after a semicolon or comma, day abbreviations, closing brackets, and the bold '**' marker that opens a highlighted name after 'the'.
Predicting the extra space token right after ' MAP' inside the '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' listing boilerplate.
Reproducing the ' MAP' token at the start of the repeated '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' boilerplate, but not the ' MAP' that follows the word 'GOOGLE'.
Completing the second half of an uncommon word or name split across tokens (MUSE-UM, Inst-itute, EUR-OPE, Wand-ering) from lexical knowledge.
Predicting the map-grid digit after a capital column letter in index entries (WahacaF[5], PlaceD[2]) and 'life' completing the recurring 'Drinking & Nightlife' header.
Predicting the period that ends a long descriptive sentence, deep into a context where sentence-final periods have already occurred.
Predicting the pound sign that begins a price anywhere in a listing (adult/child £, mains £, from £).
Predicting the full stop after a scene-final noun like 'Park', 'seafront' or 'roots' that closes a descriptive sentence.
Predicting the closing parenthesis after web addresses, dates and month abbreviations at the end of listing parentheticals, but not the ')' of the MAP boilerplate.
Predicting the newline right after a sentence-final period at the end of a paragraph, late in the context.
Completing a well-known collocation or split word from world knowledge (Great Hall, royal residence, Royal Mews, star-lings, head-land, police forces).
Predicting the possessive 's after a place or collective noun (London's, England's, the nation's, the town's).
Completing the repeated web-address ending '.co.uk' and the split 'GOOG-LE' inside the recurring listing boilerplate.
